pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever been rejected? Have you ever been overlooked? Have you ever been dismissed? It hurts. It is one of the deepest pains we can experience. But rejection is not the end of the story. Sometimes rejection is the beginning. Sometimes the one who is rejected becomes the one who delivers. Sometimes the one who is overlooked becomes the one who saves.


The Old Testament tells the story of two rejected deliverers. Moses was rejected by his people. David was rejected by his brothers. They were overlooked. They were dismissed. They were rejected. But God chose them. God called them. God used them. And they became deliverers. They became saviors. They became heroes. But they were not the ultimate deliverer. They were not the ultimate savior. They were shadows. They were echoes. They were patterns. And they point to Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who wants to understand the pattern of rejection. It is for the person who wants to see the hidden Christ. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at the lives of Moses and David. We are going to see their rejection. We are going to see their deliverance. And we are going to see how they reveal Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see rejection as the end of the story. You will see it as the beginning. You will see it as the pattern. You will see it as the blueprint. You will understand the rejected deliverer. You will understand the hidden Christ. You will understand why rejection matters today. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the one who was rejected for you.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been born into a dangerous situation? Have you ever been born into a crisis? Have you ever been born into a time of fear? Moses was. He was born in Egypt. He was born as a slave. He was born under a death sentence. The king wanted to kill all the baby boys. But God had a plan. God had a deliverer. Moses was born. He was the rejected deliverer.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Now a man of the tribe of Levi married a Levite woman, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him for three months." - Exodus 2:1-2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was born. He was a fine child. His mother hid him. She hid him for three months. She protected him. She saved him. He was the rejected deliverer.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When Herod realized that he had been outwitted by the Magi, he was furious, and he gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under..." - Matthew 2:16


Jesus was born into a dangerous situation. He was born under a death sentence. King Herod wanted to kill all the baby boys. But God had a plan. God had a deliverer. Jesus was born. He was the rejected deliverer.


The Verdict
Moses was born. Jesus was born. Both were born under a death sentence. Both were protected by God. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The deliverer is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you were born into a crisis? Do you feel like you were born into danger? Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. God has a plan. God has a deliverer. God has a purpose for your life.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the birth of Moses. Thank you for the birth of Jesus. Thank you for protecting them. Thank you for protecting me. Help me to trust your plan. Help me to trust your purpose. Help me to follow the rejected deliverer. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever needed a deliverer? Have you ever needed a savior? Have you ever needed someone to set you free? Moses was a deliverer. David was a deliverer. But they were not the ultimate deliverer. They were shadows. They were echoes. They were patterns. The ultimate deliverer is Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him." - Deuteronomy 18:15 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a deliverer. David was a deliverer. But they pointed to a greater deliverer. They pointed to Jesus. He is the ultimate deliverer.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the ultimate deliverer. He came to seek. He came to save. He came to deliver. He is the fulfillment of Moses. He is the fulfillment of David. He is the ultimate deliverer.


The Verdict
Moses was a deliverer. David was a deliverer. Jesus is the ultimate deliverer. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The deliverer is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a deliverer? Do you need a savior? Do you need to be set free? Remember Moses. Remember David. They were deliverers. But Jesus is the ultimate deliverer. He can set you free. He can save you. He can deliver you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for Moses. Thank you for David. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for the ultimate deliverer. Help me to trust the deliverer. Help me to follow the deliverer. Help me to live in the freedom of the deliverer. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Deliverer Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 days of the rejected deliverer. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every deliverer. As you read, look for the pattern. Look for the clues. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The deliverers are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The deliverers point to a person. The deliverers point to Jesus. You can understand the deliverers and still miss the ultimate deliverer. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The deliverers are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.

If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Ultimate Hero takes a 30 day look at 30 Old Testament figures who point to the rescue of Jesus. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.
